questions.question: What does the playback invariant protect first?
options: Continuous playback within startup, rebuffering, quality, and origin-protection budgets
The maximum possible resolution for every device
A single global catalog database transaction
Training recommendation models during segment download
questions.explanation: A good streaming architecture protects the viewing session and delivery reserve together; a higher rendition is useful only when it remains sustainable.

questions.question: A player has 100,000 concurrent viewers at a 5 Mbps rendition and a 1.2 peak factor. What media bandwidth should the edge plan to serve before considering overhead?
options: 60 Gbps
500 Gbps
600 Gbps
6 Tbps
questions.explanation: 100,000 viewers x 1.2 x 5 Mbps equals 600,000 Mbps, or 600 Gbps. Cache hit rate changes origin load, not the bytes delivered by the edge to viewers.

questions.question: Why can shorter media segments increase operational pressure even when video bitrate stays similar?
options: They create more segment requests per second
They make cache hits impossible
They remove the need for manifests
They force every viewer to use 4K
questions.explanation: Shorter segments improve adaptation granularity, but each viewer requests them more often, increasing request and cache-miss handling work.

questions.question: Which path should continue independently when personalization is slow or unavailable?
options: An already authorized title's segment delivery
Model retraining
Artwork experiment assignment
Homepage ranking
questions.explanation: Personalization affects discovery, but it should not sit on the media path for an active authorized playback session.

questions.question: During a cache miss storm, which mitigation best protects the origin?
options: Let every player retry origin independently
Coalesce equivalent fills, bound retries, and use safe fallback or steering
Disable all edge caches
Raise every player to a higher rendition
questions.explanation: Request coalescing and bounded retries prevent thousands of equivalent misses from amplifying into an origin overload.

questions.question: Why should an ABR controller step quality up more cautiously than it steps down?
options: A brief good throughput sample may not be sustainable, while a buffer threat needs immediate protection
Higher quality always costs less
A player cannot measure download time
Lowering quality disables caching
questions.explanation: Fast degradation helps protect buffer continuity. Delayed upgrades avoid oscillation after one favorable sample.
